source: post-merge adversarial code review of production-facing HTTP and identity boundaries

findings.problem: api/authorize-refund.js lacked PostgreSQL 23505 race recovery used by sibling idempotent handlers, allowing a concurrent winning write to surface as 503.
findings.remediation: Recover unique-violation races by re-reading the winning preview_refund_remedy row and returning the governed idempotent result, while preserving request rebound rejection.

findings.problem: The deployed preview runtime tables existed in Neon without a version-controlled migration, so fresh-database reproduction could not establish their constraints and foreign-key envelope.
findings.remediation: Introspect the existing bounded Production Neon preview schema read-only, version all seven preview runtime tables as migration 009, and execute migrations 008 and 009 in clean PostgreSQL conformance with explicit table and refund-uniqueness assertions.

findings.problem: resolveApplicationPrincipal performed deep membership/authority checks only for member: and operator: scope families; an unknown future scope family could otherwise rely only on the binding scope array.
findings.remediation: Fail closed for every unsupported scope family until that family has an explicit governed authorization contract.

exitCriteria: constitutional-conformance succeeds on the exact remediation head
fresh PostgreSQL migration execution creates all seven preview runtime tables and required refund uniqueness constraints
Vercel Production remains fail-closed after remediation work
